clue.text: Closely associated with team's account of itself?

definitions.meaning: two things set together, adjacent or working in close partnership
a team is a side, so its own story would be one told by the side about the side

explanation.surface: Someone tied closely to a club gives its own version of events.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as a side's account given by the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for things placed together or acting in close partnership.

clue.text: After spring girl losing love becomes thin

indicators.note: the girl's letters come after the spring's letters in the answer

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the girl's name

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl, jilted after spring, wastes away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes O out of ROSE, leaving RSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse and thin are synonyms for something scattered or meagre, like a thin crowd.

clue.text: Dull journal I chucked having only half read content

indicators.note: having something as its contents means the journal's letters hold the other piece
content here means what is held inside, so the half word sits within
chucked means the letter I is thrown out of the journal word

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: only half of the word read is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a boring diary after reading half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' is a noun here, the stuff held inside, not the adjective meaning satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and dreary are synonyms meaning tedious and lacking interest.

clue.text: Nasty breed — mad pet is cross

indicators.note: nasty suggests the words are treated roughly and their letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A vicious dog breed: the crazed pet is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges the letters of BREED, MAD and PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being annoyed or irritable, which is what an ill-tempered person is.

clue.text: Remain to eat a dish from the East

indicators.note: to eat means the remain word swallows the letter A

parts.note: to stay is to remain

explanation.surface: An invitation to stay and dine on something oriental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts A inside STAY, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay, skewered meat with peanut sauce, is a dish from South-East Asia.

clue.text: Money to import equipment is what monopolistic state offers

indicators.note: to import means bringing goods inside, so the money word holds the rest

parts.note: a dime is a ten-cent coin, standing for money
a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cash used to buy in kit is the policy of a controlling government.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a French loan word for state control of the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term names an economic system in which the state directs and controls trade and industry.

clue.text: Front page sequence

parts.note: a row is a line or sequence of things

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front page shows a run of stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The bow of a ship, its forward part, is the front of the vessel.

clue.text: Cut flower — it is producing allergic reaction maybe

indicators.note: cut tells us to clip the river's name by its final letter

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river, here the Rhine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sliced bloom causes someone to start sneezing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword's 'thing that flows', a river. 'Cut' trims E from RHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the nose lining is often caused by an allergy, as in hay fever, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Calculated to have suffered 50% reduction in salary for demolition job

indicators.note: in means the halved word sits inside the salary word

parts.note: a wage is pay or salary

indicators.note: a fifty per cent cut keeps only the first half of the word

parts.note: reckoned means calculated or worked out

explanation.surface: A worker's pay was halved to cover a building's destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 50% cut applies to the calculated word, not to the salary.
explanation.definitionFit: The remains left after something is wrecked are what a demolition job produces, the ruin of a structure.

clue.text: Corrective fellows interrupting female politician

indicators.note: interrupting means the fellows break into the female's name

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
men are fellows
a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Male colleagues heckle a woman MP to put her right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'female politician' looks like one unit but splits into a woman's name and a party member.
explanation.definitionFit: Something corrective serves to amend, putting right faults or errors.

clue.text: Drink you and I will keep at home

indicators.note: will keep means the pronoun holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: you and I together make we
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A couple promise to keep a bottle in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented grape juice is a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Church involved in unfortunate occult practices

indicators.note: involved in means the church letters are wrapped inside the other word

parts.note: sorry can mean unfortunate or pitiful, as in a sorry state
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church has got mixed up in some unhappy dabbling with the dark arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Witchcraft and magic are occult practices, the use of supernatural powers.

clue.text: Good introduction by e.g. Jagger may be seen as stunt

parts.note: a man named Mick, such as Mick Jagger of the Rolling Stones, would introduce himself with I'm Mick

explanation.surface: A rock star's flashy entrance could be a publicity ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' is not a beginning letter but a self-introduction; 'e.g.' marks Jagger as one example of a Mick.
explanation.definitionFit: A gimmick is a trick or device to attract attention, much like a publicity stunt.

clue.text: A deviant Mrs sacked one of the household staff

indicators.note: sacked suggests turned out and shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wayward lady of the house dismissed one of her servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges A DEVIANT MRS.
explanation.definitionFit: A female domestic servant is one of the staff employed in a household.

clue.text: Gliding along quietly, an artist's not feeling well

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
an is the indefinite article, here the letter A
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist; with the possessive S
ailing means unwell

explanation.surface: A painter drifting softly along on a glider is feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport has a person towed in a parachute, so they glide along through the air.

clue.text: The man in special unit to disrupt odd element

indicators.note: to disrupt means the group breaks into the odd word

parts.note: rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or peculiar

indicators.note: in means the man sits inside the rearranged unit
special here means altered or set out in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: he is the man

explanation.surface: A man in a special forces unit is sent to break up a peculiar group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special unit' reads as a military squad, but 'special' only signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthenium is a hard metallic chemical element of the platinum group.

clue.text: A piece of cloth in evil place? One of those places where the cloth may be found

definitions.text: One of those places where the cloth may be found

indicators.note: in means the piece of cloth sits inside the evil word

parts.note: vice is evil or wickedness
taken as written
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric in a den of iniquity; the cloth turns up in a parson's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' means the clergy, so the definition is a clergyman's house.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy are called the cloth, and a parish priest's residence is where one lives.

clue.text: Church song in which you see tot exuding heart, showing presence

indicators.note: in which you see means the trimmed word appears inside the song

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

indicators.note: exuding heart means the central letter is let out of the word

parts.note: to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum

explanation.surface: A church solo where a little child loses heart and shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' is the noun for an added-up total, not a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal magnetism, the quality called stage presence.

clue.text: What's awfully sinister about that woman? She expects to succeed

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the pronoun
awfully suggests the word is badly treated, its letters rearranged

parts.note: her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A menacing woman awaits her chance to take over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means inherit a position, not achieve success.
explanation.definitionFit: A female heir expects to succeed to a title or fortune when the holder dies.

clue.text: Wind is rising over a place where wind is never found!

indicators.note: over means the first piece sits above the second in a down entry
rising in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.words: a place where wind is never found
parts.note: the moon has no atmosphere, so no wind ever blows there

explanation.surface: A breeze gets up where no breeze can ever blow, a paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: A simoom or simoon is a hot dry desert wind of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Country needing drastic cuts? Some agree, certainly

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A debate over austerity for a debt-ridden nation finds partial agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean nation was forced into severe austerity during the eurozone debt crisis.

clue.text: A game in which kings and queens are cut short

parts.words: game in which kings and queens are
parts.note: bridge is a card game, played with a pack containing kings and queens

explanation.surface: Royalty get their reign curtailed in some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The kings and queens are playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it.

clue.text: Fouler Irish row led by leader of Dáil

indicators.note: led by means the leader's letter comes before the rest
leader of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: An Irish quarrel, started by the head of the Irish parliament, turns nastier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament; 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtier and fouler are comparatives both meaning more filthy or unpleasant.

clue.text: Famous physicist, one seen out with old group of stars

indicators.note: seen out means the letter is shown the door from the physicist's name

parts.note: Paul Dirac was a celebrated British theoretical physicist
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A noted scientist escorted out with an ageing pop band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen out' removes I from DIRAC, leaving DRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco, the Dragon, is a constellation of the northern sky.

clue.text: Too false, too dismissive of outsiders

indicators.note: dismissive of outsiders means each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being both insincere and too ready to dismiss strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissive of outsiders' leaves ALS from 'false' and O from 'too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Garbled nonsense from the old woman in capital part

indicators.note: in means the old woman sits inside the capital plus part

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
a role is a part in a play
ma is an informal word for mother, the old woman

explanation.surface: Mum, playing a role in a capital city, spouts gibberish.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a less common spelling of the usual form with no A after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: This variant of rigmarole means a long, rambling, confused story or procedure.

clue.text: Character at back of road comes to front making dash

indicators.note: character at back of names the final letter of the road word
comes to front means that letter is shifted to the start

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A figure at the rear of a road surges forward in a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character at back of' picks E, the last letter of LANE; 'comes to front' moves it to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan and dash both mean flair, energy and style.

clue.text: I am left with euphoria ultimately — it's nice when one's lost weight

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word before it
lost means the letter disappears from the word nice

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone elated at their slimming says it is lovely to have shed a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives A, the end of 'euphoria'; 'lost' removes I from NICE, giving NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight and significance are synonyms, as in a matter of great weight or consequence.
